text:
alex: customer acme-42 hit a parse error in json-mode when streaming through their updated edge proxy. client sees a partial JSON object (ends mid-key) and then the connection closes. they get parse failures and retry loops -> billing spike :grimacing:

maria: can you paste the raw SSE payload that the client received? also which API params (model, mode=json_schema, any stream flags)?

alex: pasted below (redacted):
```
data: {"id":"resp_01F", "choices": [ { "delta": { "content": { "name": "widget", "value": "large", "meta": { "size": 12,"color": "blue" } } } } ]}
data: [DONE]
```
But the client actually only received up to `"size": 12` and then a hard EOF. No closing braces.
Headers they observed: `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Connection: keep-alive` (their proxy rewrites keepalive to 3s).

chris: @maria checking our LB/runtime logs for that time window. do we see an upstream FIN or any 50x? :eyes:

inbox-bot: Deploy 1701 finished on runtime-01 at 2026-03-15T02:10:22Z

maria: looked at runtime logs — we flushed full chunks to the LB and we closed normally after sending [DONE]. no early close on our side. however there's a TCP FIN from 10.2.8.9 (customer edge) at 1769999988 indicating the proxy terminated the connection mid-stream.

alex: customer reported this started after they moved traffic to their Fastly config and enabled aggressive keepalive timeouts. they can repro with curl: `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://api.redwood.com/v1/responses/stream -d '{"input":"...","mode":"json_schema"}'` — stream cuts after ~2.8s consistently.

denise: they're also reporting a billing spike because their client retries on parse errors. can we offer temporary credit or an immediate workaround?

maria: immediate mitigation options for customer: 1) switch to non-streaming API until proxy keepalive is fixed; 2) raise keepalive/buffer settings on their Fastly edge; 3) add client-side tolerant parser that can retry/resume (hard). server-side mitigation idea: heartbeat tokens (SSE comments) to keep proxy alive.

chris: adding heartbeats server-side might help. we could emit a `:heartbeat

` SSE comment every 1s (config flag `sse.keepalive_interval`). low risk but needs eng-runtime signoff and a canary. tagging @eng-runtime to review.

eng-runtime: logging this. heartbeats are a common compatibility shim for aggressive proxies. two concerns: 1) extra traffic for very high QPS tenants, 2) could change how some clients buffer. we'll start a canary with heartbeat enabled on a small runtime pool and measure.

alex: customer agreed to switch to non-streaming for now while we test canary. they've asked for a clear repro to hand back to Fastly ops. i've attached the curl example, sample SSE capture, and our tcpdump snippet.

maria: i'll open a support ticket (P1) with logs, tcpdump, runtime trace_id, and recommended mitigations. also noting model=gpt-extended-3, streaming=true, mode=json_schema. escalated to eng-runtime for canary.

denise: i'll loop in billing to discuss one-off credit for retries.

chris: follow-up action items: (1) eng-runtime to run heartbeat canary, (2) support to provide customer-facing repro + temp workaround, (3) billing to evaluate credit.

alex: thanks everyone. I'll post customer acceptance once they validate non-streaming path. :thumbsup:
